messages.subject: Unfamiliar error message: Error in E.inv %*% B0 : requires numeric/complex matrix/vector arguments
parts:
Hi,

I am running a simulation study which, due to certain combinations of conditions, generates quite a bit of model non-convergence at small sample sizes. However, I got the error message in the subject line for the first time today and have never seen it before. A quick google search turns up 0 results. Could someone please tell me what's going wrong? The data I'm trying to fit the model to are attached here, and the syntax is reproduced below.

Thanks,
Jon

load(<path to data file>)
fitModel <- 'eta1 =~ NA*y1 + 1*y2 + y3 + y4
             eta2 =~ NA*y4 + 1*y5 + y6 + y7
             eta3 =~ NA*y6 + NA*y7 + 1*y8 + y9
             eta1 ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
             eta2 ~ eta1 + x1 + x3
             eta3 ~ eta2 + x1 + x3'
fit <- sem(fitModel,data=data,estimator="MLR")

messages.author: 885539f3f5ae8fd5
messages.subject: Re: Unfamiliar error message: Error in E.inv %*% B0 : requires numeric/complex matrix/vector arguments
parts:
Ok, I think the problem stems from the attempted computation of the Huber-White SE, which is the default method when estimator="MLR" if I'm not mistaken. I think the error stems from the function lav_model_nvcov_robust_sandwich, where near the end of the function appears the line
NVarCov <- E.inv %*% B0 %*% E.inv
I'm not sure what to do about this -- is this just an example of lavaan not being able to compute the standard errors of the parameter estimates of the model? Or is this symptomatic of a larger problem? In my simulation I don't really care about the parameter estimates, only the chi-squared statistic and some fit indices based on it, so should I be safe if I ignore this problem when it occurs?

Actually, if I don't care about the parameter estimates, I can just specify SE="none" right? That won't affect anything relating to the test statistic or fit indices?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Unfamiliar error message: Error in E.inv %*% B0 : requires numeric/complex matrix/vector arguments
parts:
> fitModel <-'eta1 =~ NA*y1 + 1*y2 + y3 + y4
> eta2 =~ NA*y4 + 1*y5 + y6 + y7
> eta3 =~ NA*y6 + NA*y7 + 1*y8 + y9
> eta1 ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
> eta2 ~ eta1 + x1 + x3
> eta3 ~ eta2 + x1 + x3'
> fit <-sem(fitModel,data=data,estimator="MLR")

You need to fix the metric of the latent variables. Try

fit <-sem(fitModel,data=data,estimator="MLR", std.lv = TRUE)

Nevertheless, the error should have been catched earlier, and I will try
to handle this setting better.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Unfamiliar error message: Error in E.inv %*% B0 : requires numeric/complex matrix/vector arguments
parts:
On 06/13/2015 03:52 PM, Jon wrote:
> Ok, I think the problem stems from the attempted computation of the
> Huber-White SE, which is the default method when estimator="MLR" if I'm
> not mistaken. I think the error stems from the function
> lav_model_nvcov_robust_sandwich, where near the end of the function
> appears the line
> |
> NVarCov<-E.inv %*%B0 %*%E.inv

Yes. E.inv (the inverse of the information matrix) is not defined
(because your model is not identified), and this fails.
> I'm not sure what to do about this
Be sure you fit identified models.

> Actually, if I don't care about the parameter estimates, I can just
> specify SE="none" right? That won't affect anything relating to the test
> statistic or fit indices?

It is just the opposite. Setting se="none" might give you parameter
estimates, but no standard errors. You will not be able to get a robust
(scaled) test statistic either. Because this needs E.inv again.

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Unfamiliar error message: Error in E.inv %*% B0 : requires numeric/complex matrix/vector arguments
parts: I actually thought that I had been fixing the metric of one of the factor loadings on each factor (y2, y5, and y7) by specifying 1* before each of them, which would mean I don't need to fix the metric of the latent variables, no? Maybe the syntax I used for that wasn't correct.

The model specification is fine, but because lavaan by default will fix the loading of the first variable you mention to 1 to set the scale (i.e., freely estimate latent variances), that might unnecessarily conflict with your model syntax.  Wouldn't it be easier to simply put the marker variable first?

fitModel <- 'eta1 =~ y2 + y1 + y3 + y4
             eta2 =~ y5 + y4 + y6 + y7
             eta3 =~ y8 + y6 + y7 + y9

eta1 ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
             eta2 ~ eta1 + x1 + x3
             eta3 ~ eta2 + x1 + x3'
on iterations where the model fit completed without error or warning

In those cases, E.inv is available, so of course you can get the scaled statistic.

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Unfamiliar error message: Error in E.inv %*% B0 : requires numeric/complex matrix/vector arguments
parts: unless I'm misunderstanding, the model is identified (the syntax does specify that enough parameters are fixed, and also if the model weren't identified then all iterations would fail), so what's causing this error in the first place?

Actually, I think the reason your model is not identified is because there is only one unique indicator of eta2 (the one with the fixed loading).  The other indicators of eta2 have cross-loadings one eta1 or eta3, so I don't think you have enough information to get a unique solution.  To check this, I tried simulating (N = 100 normal) data from your measurement model (with some arbitrary population parameters, see below), and then fitting the measurement part of your fitModel to the data.  It converged, but convergence is only a necessary (not sufficient) condition to say the model was adequately identified.  To check identification, you can then fit the same model to the model-implied covariance matrix, and you should be able to get the exact same solution (because you know the model fits perfectly to the model-implied moments).  When I fit it again, the factor loadings were all the same, but the latent (co)variances and error variances were a bit different.  When I fit the model to those model-implied moments, the estimates changed yet again.  This is a sign that the model is not actually identified, even though the estimation algorithm managed to find what appeared to be a maximum likelihood solution.

Terry

fitModel <- '
eta1 =~ NA*y1 + 1*y2 + y3 + y4
eta2 =~ NA*y4 + 1*y5 + y6 + y7
eta3 =~ NA*y6 + NA*y7 + 1*y8 + y9

'

popModel <- '
eta1 =~ .8*y1 + 1*y2 + .8*y3 + .8*y4
eta2 =~ .8*y4 + 1*y5 + .8*y6 + .8*y7
eta3 =~ .8*y6 + .8*y7 + 1*y8 + .8*y9
y1 ~~ .5*y1
y2 ~~ .5*y2
y3 ~~ .5*y3
y4 ~~ .5*y4
y5 ~~ .5*y5
y6 ~~ .5*y6
y7 ~~ .5*y7
y8 ~~ .5*y8
y9 ~~ .5*y9
eta1 ~~ 1*eta1 + .4*eta2 + .5*eta3
eta2 ~~ 1*eta2 + .3*eta3
eta3 ~~ 1*eta3
'

dat <- simulateData(popModel, model.type = "cfa", meanstructure = FALSE, sample.nobs = 100L)

fit <- cfa(fitModel, data = dat)
summary(fit)

fitAgain <- cfa(fitModel, sample.nobs = 100L, sample.cov = lavInspect(fit, "cov.all")[1:9,1:9])
summary(fitAgain)

fitYetAgain <- cfa(fitModel, sample.nobs = 100L, sample.cov = lavInspect(fitAgain, "cov.all")[1:9,1:9])
summary(fitYetAgain)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Unfamiliar error message: Error in E.inv %*% B0 : requires numeric/complex matrix/vector arguments
parts:
On 06/12/2015 10:24 PM, Jon wrote:
> fitModel <-'eta1 =~ NA*y1 + 1*y2 + y3 + y4
> eta2 =~ NA*y4 + 1*y5 + y6 + y7
> eta3 =~ NA*y6 + NA*y7 + 1*y8 + y9
> eta1 ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
> eta2 ~ eta1 + x1 + x3
> eta3 ~ eta2 + x1 + x3'
> fit <-sem(fitModel,data=data,estimator="MLR")

Reading this back while browsing the archives...

The problem is that this model is not identified. You need to fix the
variance of the exogenous latent variable (eta3). Adding a line

eta3 ~~ 1*eta3

works. In recent versions (0.5-20), the original model will not produce
the error message, but spit out many warning messages (hinting at the
under-identified nature of this model).

Yves.
